$comment: Curated GATE Computer Science and Information Technology curriculum.
Source: the GATE 2026 syllabus published by IIT Guwahati, the organising
institute -- CS_2026_Syllabus.pdf for sections 1-10 and GA_2026_Syllabus.pdf
for General Aptitude, which is part of the CS paper.
Transcription rules, applied uniformly so the file stays checkable against
the source:
* One subject per official section. `position` is the official section
number; General Aptitude has no number in the CS paper and is appended
last.
* A subject `description` is the section's official text, verbatim.
* Topics are that text split at the delimiter the section itself uses: the
named area for Engineering Mathematics and General Aptitude, the
semicolon for Computer Networks, the sentence elsewhere.
* `is_trackable` is false for a topic that only groups subtopics and true
for a topic a learner studies directly.
* Wording is unchanged. The only normalisation is U+2010 HYPHEN to ASCII
'-', so codes and names stay typeable.
`topic_relationships` is empty on purpose. The official syllabus states no
prerequisite or sequencing order between topics, and inventing one would
present an assistant's guess as curriculum. The seed supports relationships
so a curated, reviewed set can be added later without a code change.
program_name: GATE Computer Science and Information Technology
program_description: The Computer Science and Information Technology (CS) paper of the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering.
source_reference: GATE 2026 CS and GA syllabus, IIT Guwahati (organising institute): https://gate2026.iitg.ac.in/doc/GATE2026_Syllabus/CS_2026_Syllabus.pdf and https://gate2026.iitg.ac.in/doc/GATE2026_Syllabus/GA_2026_Syllabus.pdf

subjects.name: Engineering Mathematics
subjects.description: Discrete Mathematics: Propositional and first order logic. Sets, relations, functions, partial orders and lattices. Monoids, Groups. Graphs: connectivity, matching, colouring. Combinatorics: counting, recurrence relations, generating functions. Linear Algebra: Matrices, determinants, system of linear equations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, LU decomposition. Calculus: Limits, continuity and differentiability, Maxima and minima, Mean value theorem, Integration. Probability and Statistics: Random variables, Uniform, normal, exponential, Poisson and binomial distributions. Mean, median, mode and standard deviation. Conditional probability and Bayes theorem.

subjects.name: Digital Logic
subjects.description: Boolean algebra. Combinational and sequential circuits. Minimization. Number representations and computer arithmetic (fixed and floating point).

topics.name: Number representations and computer arithmetic (fixed and floating point)

subjects.name: Computer Organization and Architecture
subjects.description: Machine instructions and addressing modes. ALU, data-path and control unit. Instruction pipelining, pipeline hazards. Memory hierarchy: cache, main memory and secondary storage; I/O interface (interrupt and DMA mode).

topics.name: Memory hierarchy: cache, main memory and secondary storage; I/O interface (interrupt and DMA mode)

subjects.name: Programming and Data Structures
subjects.description: Programming in C. Recursion. Arrays, stacks, queues, linked lists, trees, binary search trees, binary heaps, graphs.

topics.name: Arrays, stacks, queues, linked lists, trees, binary search trees, binary heaps, graphs

subjects.name: Algorithms
subjects.description: Searching, sorting, hashing. Asymptotic worst case time and space complexity. Algorithm design techniques: greedy, dynamic programming and divide-and-conquer. Graph traversals, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths.

topics.name: Asymptotic worst case time and space complexity

subjects.name: Theory of Computation
subjects.description: Regular expressions and finite automata. Context-free grammars and push-down automata. Regular and context-free languages, pumping lemma. Turing machines and undecidability.

topics.name: Regular and context-free languages, pumping lemma

subjects.name: Compiler Design
subjects.description: Lexical analysis, parsing, syntax-directed translation. Runtime environments. Intermediate code generation. Local optimisation, Data flow analyses: constant propagation, liveness analysis, common sub expression elimination.

topics.name: Local optimisation, Data flow analyses: constant propagation, liveness analysis, common sub expression elimination

subjects.name: Operating System
subjects.description: System calls, processes, threads, inter-process communication, concurrency and synchronization. Deadlock. CPU and I/O scheduling. Memory management and virtual memory. File systems.

topics.name: System calls, processes, threads, inter-process communication, concurrency and synchronization

subjects.name: Databases
subjects.description: ER-model. Relational model: relational algebra, tuple calculus, SQL. Integrity constraints, normal forms. File organization, indexing (e.g., B and B+ trees). Transactions and concurrency control.

topics.name: Relational model: relational algebra, tuple calculus, SQL
File organization, indexing (e.g., B and B+ trees)

subjects.name: Computer Networks
subjects.description: Concept of layering: OSI and TCP/IP Protocol Stacks; Basics of packet, circuit and virtual circuit-switching; Data link layer: framing, error detection, Medium Access Control, Ethernet bridging; Routing protocols: shortest path, flooding, distance vector and link state routing; Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation, Basics of IP support protocols (ARP, DHCP, ICMP), Network Address Translation (NAT); Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets; Application layer protocols: DNS, SMTP, HTTP, FTP, Email.

subjects.name: General Aptitude
subjects.description: Verbal Aptitude: Basic English grammar: tenses, articles, adjectives, prepositions, conjunctions, verb-noun agreement, and other parts of speech. Basic vocabulary: words, idioms, and phrases in context. Reading and comprehension, Narrative sequencing. Quantitative Aptitude: Data interpretation: data graphs (bar graphs, pie charts, and other graphs representing data), 2- and 3-dimensional plots, maps, and tables. Numerical computation and estimation: ratios, percentages, powers, exponents and logarithms, permutations and combinations, and series. Mensuration and geometry. Elementary statistics and probability. Analytical Aptitude: Logic: deduction and induction, Analogy, Numerical relations and reasoning. Spatial Aptitude: Transformation of shapes: translation, rotation, scaling, mirroring, assembling, and grouping. Paper folding, cutting, and patterns in 2 and 3 dimensions.
